messages:
anna_support: customer says refund endpoint (/v1/actions/refund) returned 200 but instead of issuing a bank refund we ended up applying a loyalty credit to the account. user id: user_92fa, request id: req_7b3c. amount: 42.00 USD. can we escalate?

anna_support: repro curl we used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/actions/refund \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"user_id":"user_92fa","amount":42.00,"currency":"USD","reason":"overcharge","refund_method":"original_payment"}'
```

mike_runtime: can you paste the router trace/log for req_7b3c? need to see which tool/compiler matched. :eyes:

anna_support: pasted below (sanitized to remove PII):
```
[router] req=req_7b3c model=gptx-infer router_v=2026-02-14  selector_scores={"apply_loyalty_credit":0.872, "process_refund":0.853, "create_credit_note":0.512} selected=apply_loyalty_credit reason_tokens=["credit","apply","amount"]
[tool-invoker] selected_tool=apply_loyalty_credit args={"amount":42.0,"currency":"USD","note":"overcharge"}
[api] response=200 body={"status":"ok","applied":true,"type":"loyalty_credit","balance_delta":42.0}
```

sam_engineer: interesting — scores are very close. router is currently a token/alias + signature similarity model. both tools share almost identical required fields so signature similarity is high.

jess_product: fyi we rolled in an alias update last week that added the token "credit" to the loyalty tool aliases (per request to surface promos). that probably moved its score up. :grimacing:

mike_runtime: root cause hypothesis: alias overlap + identical minimal schema means the selector leans on token hits. because the payload didn't include an explicit refund_method recognized by refund tool (we use "refund_method" optional field but router weights optional fields low), loyalty wins.

mike_runtime: quick mitigation options:
- restore alias change (remove "credit") from loyalty tool to reduce token hits
- add required discriminator field to process_refund (e.g., require refund_method) and bump its signature weight
- short-term hotfix: prefer tools with name containing "refund" when request path is /actions/refund (route-based bias)

anna_support: customer needs fix ASAP, they already had money hold. which is fastest?

mike_runtime: fastest is route-based bias patch (small config change) — I can push a canary in the next deploy window and roll to 5% traffic for hosted API.

sam_engineer: also recommend adding a validation check in invoker: if selected tool == apply_loyalty_credit and request_path contains "/refund" then throw validation warning and escalate instead of auto-invoking. prevents silent misroutes while we work on selector.

jess_product: agree. we'll revert the alias change in the next release and update docs.

anna_support: can you share rollback/canary plan and ETA so I can tell the customer?

mike_runtime: plan:
1) apply route-bias config at 5% canary (team=runtime) - ETA 30m
2) monitor traces for req_7b3c-like patterns and roll to 100% if no regressions - ETA additional 30m
3) follow up PR to require refund_method in process_refund schema + revert loyalty alias - ETA today EOD

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary:runtime-route-bias-2026-02-14 by mike_runtime (req: deploy_8821)

mike_runtime: hooked up a synthetic check that hits /actions/refund with the same payload and asserts selected_tool==process_refund. initial canary logs look good. will update in 10m. :thumbsup:

anna_support: customer notified: "we've identified the issue and are deploying a canary fix, you should see the proper refund applied shortly. we'll confirm when complete."

sam_engineer: long-term items tracked: (1) add alias collision detection to onboarding, (2) improve signature weighting for optional vs required fields, (3) invoker path-aware validation rules.

mike_runtime: assigning follow-ups: mike_runtime -> hotfix + canary, jess_product -> alias revert PR, sam_engineer -> selector weighting ticket.

anna_support: marking this thread as escalated -> in-progress. will post final status when resolved.
